messages:
Diego (Eng): FYI I'm planning a temporary move to Guam from 2026-09-01 for ~95 days to help with family logistics. Quick list: 1) Is WFH stipend payable while I'm on Guam? 2) Any payroll/state/territory withholding or nexus implications? 3) Health/benefits concerns? 4) Can Facilities ship a printer and a monitor there?
Priya (People Ops): Thanks for the heads-up Diego. Short answers: WFH stipend can be paid for temporary international U.S. territories but we need the relocate form. Because this is ~95 days (over 90) we'll need to escalate to Payroll + Legal for nexus/territory review. Please don't book anything until Payroll/Legal confirm.
Ravi (Payroll): Guam is a U.S. territory with different tax rules (income tax there applies to Guam-source income). Practically: if you are physically working from Guam >90 days, Payroll will open a withholding review. We may need to adjust your federal/territory withholding and issue local reporting. Also note any local payroll filings for the company if more employees start working there.
Saanvi (Benefits): Benefits coverage generally continues for U.S. territories but network availability and prescription coverage vary. For Guam specifically, check telehealth and out-of-network claims; some plans treat Guam differently. If you need urgent care while there, DM me and we'll walk through options.
Marcus (Legal): From a legal/nexus perspective: stays >90 days increase the chance of creating a taxable presence depending on the volume of work and client interactions. We need a short memo describing activities (are you meeting clients there? Shipping or storing equipment? Engaging collaborators locally?). Please don't run prod demos or ship model checkpoints to local contractors without Legal sign-off.
Diego (Eng): Not meeting clients, purely family & remote work. No equipment shipments planned initially, just personal laptop. I do plan to run daily standups and occasional product demos to US-based customers (video calls).
Marcus (Legal): Video calls to US customers are low risk but the duration (>90 days) pushes this into the "review required" bucket. Priya, please route Diego's relocate form + a one-paragraph activity note to Legal so we can document and clear this.
Priya (People Ops): Will do. Diego, please complete the short relocate form and check the box for ">90 days" so it auto-flags Legal/Payroll. Link: https://redwood.internal/relocate-form. Also include shipping requests for Facilities on the form.
Leo (Facilities): We can ship a monitor and a small printer for temporary assignment. We'll treat it as loaned equipment; please choose "temporary equipment" on the asset form. Recipient signature required on delivery in Guam; we can coordinate insurance for shipping. Note: international shipping timelines vary (4-14 business days).
Diego (Eng): Thanks. Anything about retirement / 401(k) or payroll deductions?
Ravi (Payroll): 401(k) deductions and employer match continue as usual while you're an active U.S. employee. However, local tax treatment could affect net pay; we will provide a simulated payroll run for the months in Guam so you can see net pay impact before you leave. Also, if you receive any local payments or contractor income in Guam, that's separate and may trigger filings.
tax-bot: Automated note: Employees flagged as working >90 days outside their home state/territory will be reviewed for withholding adjustments. Submit relocation with ">90 days" flag for automatic ticket creation (TAX-GBM-001).
Diego (Eng): Form submitted and checked >90 days. Added activity note: "family caregiving, standard remote engineering work, no in-person client meetings." Also requested monitor + printer.
Priya (People Ops): Got it. We'll coordinate with Legal and Payroll and get back within 3 business days. If Legal deems it high-risk we may need to limit certain customer-facing activities or run an interim payroll configuration. Keep us posted on travel bookings.
Marcus (Legal): We'll review the memo. If approved, Legal will issue a clearance note and any required internal mitigations (e.g., no local contracting, limited data transfers).
Saanvi (Benefits): Once Legal/Payroll clear, I'll check plan network for Guam and DM you any notes about prescriptions/clinics.
Diego (Eng): Appreciate it. I'll wait for the clearance before finalizing flights. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
